ratings_why.fun: Borrowing the shop's best text and growing it with Hob, Veil-Stitcher and Hollin is a joy to draft, but a Lady board with five texts is hard to read at a glance.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7: no tribe today trades units into the shop or joins other tribes' synergies, and Exchange plus a Guise that brings its tribe does both, which is the swapped-at-birth folklore made into rules.

verdict_why: One real wording fix: "Guise" names both a unit's own text and the text a Changeling wears, so Wicker Moll and the Placement Officer can be read two ways.

points.text: "That unit's Guise" means its own text, but "its Guise" also means the text a Changeling wears. When you sell a Changeling in a Guise, Wicker Moll's Stock could wear either; give the worn one its own word, or say "its text" on Moll, the Stand-In and the Kit.
Placement Officer moves the given unit's Guise away, but Exchange says you can buy that unit back "with its buffs and Guise". Say which wins: does the buy-back come home bare?
Penny Second reads well, but say that her copied text survives when the enemy loses its own, so players know the Mire really moves to her.
Weeks-Old Hob says "a unit beside it" and can have two; "choose a unit beside it" removes the guess.

Grandfer Acorn is the eggshell test in the folklore; a small unmasking beat (his Guise drops when a Changeling beside him changes Guise, and he gains for it) would put the seed's best-known tale on a card.

standouts.why: Wicker Moll leaving a Stock in the sold unit's slot is the folklore exactly, and a player sees it happen.
Pip Unlike's mirror-backwards copy is short, funny and makes a new lane for Pass.
Clerk of Exchanges is one plain line that opens the shop as a trading partner.

weakest.why: The Lady wears every Guise: the strongest fantasy but the hardest card on the board to read in a fight.
Coat-Peg Steward's moving of permanent stats is hard to track once units round-trip through the shop.
The Matron is a generic count-the-tribes buffer; it carries little of the changeling feel.

flags.note: Selling a Changeling in a Guise: does the Stock wear its own text or the Guise it wore?
Conflicts with Exchange's buy-back keeping the Guise.
Five or more texts on one unit; the UI cost is the biggest in the tribe.
With the Lady, doubles every borrowed fight trigger; the high roll to watch.
